solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Irresponsible benefit given out freely? (4-3-7)

blocks.note: describes a feckless, useless idler
read literally: a GOOD (benefit) handed out FOR NOTHING (free)

annotation.surface: A complaint about handouts that are too easily given.
annotation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into its parts: a good given for nothing; the question mark flags that pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a feckless idler lacks all sense of responsibility, and the phrase split up describes a benefit handed out free.

entries.clue: Pleased revised notes talk about case (9,3)

indicators.note: notes that are revised are rewritten in a new order
talk comes round, turning back on itself

blocks.note: glad = pleased
NOTES rearranged
gab = idle talk; turned round to BAG

annotation.surface: Someone happy with the new notes for a talk about a legal case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case' sounds like a lawsuit after talk of notes, but it means luggage. A Gladstone bag is a hinged leather travelling bag named after the Victorian prime minister.
annotation.definitionFit: A Gladstone bag is a kind of case for carrying belongings.

entries.clue: Get round former pupil by half term (7)

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil
via = by way of
the first half of TERM

annotation.surface: An old pupil dropping by the school during the half-term holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half term' reads as the British school holiday midway through a term, but it asks for half the word TERM.
annotation.definitionFit: To obviate a difficulty is to get round it, removing the need to face it.

entries.clue: Leading newspaper charged by taxman in US (5)

indicators.note: the newspaper is filled, like a charged glass, with the taxman

blocks.note: FT = Financial Times
the Internal Revenue Service, the American tax authority; it goes inside FT

annotation.surface: A top paper being billed by the American tax authorities.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leading newspaper' looks like one phrase, but 'Leading' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Leading and first both mean ahead of all others.

entries.clue: One will almost blunder into bit of light banter (8)

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its last letter
the first pieces go inside the next

blocks.note: a ray is a thin beam of light
I'LL = I will, with one as I
ERR without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone nearly slipping up in a moment of light-hearted chat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One will' is compressed into I'LL, with one as I. RA(ILL ER)Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing, which is banter.

entries.clue: Nervously excited about move, in a cautious way (2,4)

blocks.note: on = about, as in a talk on a subject
to edge is to move slowly and carefully

annotation.surface: A jittery person moving warily.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition and the wordplay describe the same nervous figure, which hides where one ends.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: being tense and jumpy, like someone balanced at a cliff's brink.

entries.clue: Vital sign that’s beginning to divide two judges (5,4)

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken
the letter splits the two judges apart

blocks.note: to hear a case is to judge it
first letter of THAT'S
to rate is to judge

annotation.surface: A medical sign that splits a pair of judges.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Two judges' are two verbs, HEAR and RATE, not two people on a bench.
annotation.definitionFit: Heart rate is one of the vital signs a doctor checks, along with temperature and breathing.

entries.clue: Most within reach of place of birth receiving attention (7)

indicators.note: the nest takes the other piece inside it

blocks.note: a nest is where chicks are born
to give ear is to pay attention; it goes inside NEST

annotation.surface: A birthplace getting the most attention.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Place of birth' suggests a town or hospital, but it is a bird's nest.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the superlative of near, the closest thing to hand.

entries.clue: Make public secrets regularly withheld by counsel (9)

indicators.note: every other letter is taken
the letters are held inside the counsel

blocks.note: to counsel is to advise
sEcReTs, even letters; placed inside ADVISE

annotation.surface: A lawyer keeping secrets back, and then going public.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Counsel' looks like a barrister, which suits secrets withheld, but it is the verb ADVISE. ADV(ERT)ISE.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to publicise a product or notice is to announce it openly.

entries.clue: Not at home a week a year (4)

blocks.note: used as printed
w = week, the standard abbreviation
used as printed
y = year

annotation.surface: Someone who is out of the house one week in every year.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a holiday allowance, which disguises four separate letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who is out or travelling is absent from their house, and a team playing on the other side's ground is also said to be playing there.

entries.clue: Forthright genius dismissing one mad genius? (12)

indicators.note: the named letter is sent away from the word

blocks.note: frank = forthright
EINSTEIN, the proverbial genius, with one I removed

annotation.surface: A plain-speaking genius getting rid of a crazed rival.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mad genius' is Victor Frankenstein, the scientist who built a creature in Mary Shelley's novel; the question mark admits the definition is a description, not a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Mary Shelley's Victor, who builds a living creature, is the archetypal crazed scientist.

entries.clue: Kick-off ends in furious fight round pitch (5)

indicators.note: the last letters of the words are taken
the letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: last letters of furiouS and fighT
pitch is a black sticky substance; it goes inside ST

annotation.surface: A football match that opens with a brawl on the field.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' reads as a football field after 'Kick-off', but it is the black sticky stuff.
annotation.definitionFit: A football term standing for the beginning of anything.

entries.clue: Many miles they staggered in disposing of grail (5,4)

indicators.note: the letters stagger about into a new order
one set of letters sits inside the other
disposing is arranging, so GRAIL is rearranged

blocks.note: GRAIL rearranged; the outer piece
THEY rearranged; placed inside

annotation.surface: Knights stumbling a long way while getting rid of the Holy Grail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Disposing of' suggests throwing away, but here it means arranging. LIG(HTYE)AR.
annotation.definitionFit: A light year is the distance light travels in a year, about six trillion miles.

entries.clue: Reduced waste following public proposal (8)

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter
the waste comes after the public piece

blocks.note: overt = open, public
UREA, a waste product in urine, cut short

annotation.surface: A cut in waste after a public consultation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Waste' is a chemical here: urea, the body's nitrogen waste.
annotation.definitionFit: An opening approach or offer to another party, as in making friendly advances.

entries.clue: Learner admitted to becoming keen on lecture (7-2)

indicators.note: the learner is let inside the phrase

blocks.note: taking to = becoming keen on
L = learner, as on L-plates; it goes inside TAKING TO

annotation.surface: A student getting interested in a lecture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lecture' looks like the thing the learner is keen on, but it is the definition, as in a telling-off.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a telling-off delivered at length, as a scolding lecture is.

entries.clue: Arthur Brown keeps material in check (6)

indicators.note: the brown holds the other piece inside

blocks.note: tan = brown
the name Arthur shortened to its first three letters; kept inside TAN

annotation.surface: A man called Arthur Brown keeping someone under control.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arthur Brown' looks like one person's name, and 'in check' like restraint; check is a squared pattern.
annotation.definitionFit: Tartan is cloth woven in a check pattern.

entries.clue: Bewitching creature that Parisian married, stopping return of curse (5,3)

indicators.note: the word is put into French
the letter plugs the gap in the next word
the word comes back, reading right to left

blocks.note: que = that in French
bane = curse; reversed to ENAB
m = married; it goes inside ENAB

annotation.surface: A Frenchman's wife interrupting an old grudge coming back.
annotation.walkthrough: Queen Mab is the fairy queen of dreams in Mercutio's speech in Romeo and Juliet. QUE + EN(M)AB.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the fairy midwife of dreams is an enchanting, spell-casting being.

entries.clue: Preserve large plant opened by business graduate (6)

indicators.note: the tree is opened up to take the graduate inside

blocks.note: an elm is a large tree
MBA = Master of Business Administration; it goes inside ELM

annotation.surface: A business graduate cutting open a big plant to keep it alive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large plant' is a tree, not a factory.
annotation.definitionFit: Treating a corpse with chemicals so it does not decay keeps it intact.

entries.clue: Speculative buyer charged item as means to make money (7)

blocks.note: a bull buys shares expecting prices to rise
an ion is an electrically charged particle

annotation.surface: A stock-market speculator whose purchases are a way to profit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests a price, and 'make money' suggests profit; the money here is literally minted from bullion.
annotation.definitionFit: Bullion is gold or silver in bulk, the raw material from which coins are made.

entries.clue: Able to figure out true name (8)

indicators.note: the letters are worked out into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Someone able to work out a person's real name.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure out' looks like one phrasal verb, but 'figure' ends the definition, meaning to do arithmetic.
annotation.definitionFit: Being numerate means able to work with numbers, to figure.

entries.clue: How one deals with unknown quantities? (7)

definitions.text: How one deals with unknown quantities?

blocks.note: reads as coping with something; really the method or branch of study used to handle it
reads as unpredictable people or things; really the letters like x and y standing for numbers not yet known

annotation.surface: Advice on coping with situations you cannot predict.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads like advice on handling the unforeseen; 'unknown quantities' is literally the mathematics term for the values x and y stand for.
annotation.definitionFit: Algebra is the branch of mathematics that works with unknown quantities.

entries.clue: Correct wordplay is hard (6)

blocks.note: a pun is a play on words
used as printed
H = hard, as on pencils

annotation.surface: A remark that getting wordplay right is difficult.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Correct' reads as an adjective, but it is the verb, to discipline.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb has an old sense of disciplining someone for a fault, as in a house of correction.

entries.clue: Change a result that is not working (2,7)

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
i.e. = that is; also part of the fodder

annotation.surface: A plea to alter an outcome that has failed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not working' looks like something broken, but it means off duty.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for being free from work or duties, off the clock.

entries.clue: Salary used to be supplemented by tips from good employer (5)

indicators.note: the extra letters are added inside the word
the tip of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: was = used to be
first letters of Good and Employer; they go inside WAS

annotation.surface: Pay that is topped up by tips from a generous boss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tips' look like gratuities, which fits salary, but they are first letters. WA(GE)S.
annotation.definitionFit: Wages are the pay a worker earns, a salary.

entries.clue: Server disconnected from current electricity generator (5)

indicators.note: the letter is cut away from the word

blocks.note: a waiter serves at table
I is the symbol for electric current; removed from WAITER

annotation.surface: A waiter unplugged from the mains near a generator.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' pairs with electricity in the surface, but it is just the letter I. Water drives hydroelectric turbines.
annotation.definitionFit: Flowing water generates hydroelectric power.

entries.clue: Chorus perform wrong note (4)

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong
G is a musical note

annotation.surface: A choir hitting a bad note.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'wrong note' look like one mistake, but it is two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Vocal performance is the whole business of a choir.

entries.clue: Confession of drug smuggler about LSD never changing (9)

indicators.note: the confession goes round the drug

blocks.note: I'M MULE: a mule is a drug courier
a tab is a dose of LSD; it goes inside IM MU LE

annotation.surface: A drug runner admitting to carrying acid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Confession' is a literal admission, I'M MULE. IM MU(TAB)LE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fixed and unalterable.

entries.clue: Too enthusiastic about growth of legal profession? (4,3,7)

blocks.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
the Bar is the profession of barristers
a gain is an increase

annotation.surface: Someone overexcited about lawyers multiplying.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Too enthusiastic' reads as one phrase, but 'Too' alone is the definition, meaning also.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning in addition, as well.
